chapterNote: The entrance liturgy — the question a pilgrim asked at the gate and the answer the priest gave back. Who may be a guest in Your tent, LORD? Who may settle on Your holy hill? The answer is not a ritual checklist but a character sketch in eleven strokes: the one who walks whole, does what is right, and tells the truth inside his own heart; whose tongue does not go out spying for gossip, who does no harm to his neighbor and will not pick up a slur against him; who despises what is contemptible and honors those who fear the LORD; who swears to his own loss and does not change his mind; who does not lend at biting interest and will not take a bribe against the innocent. Then the promise: the one who does these things will never be shaken. It reads like a description of Christ, which is the only way any of us stand on that hill — and, once we do, it reads like the life He makes in us. James 3 and Romans 13 are both here in seed.

1.text: A psalm of David. O LORD, who may sojourn in Your tent? Who may dwell on Your holy hill?
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of David. LORD [YHWH], who shall abide ['sojourn', gur, the KJV margin] in Your tabernacle [ohel — tent]? who shall dwell [shakan] in Your holy [qodesh] hill [har]?
1.notes: The gate-question: mi-yagur be-oholekha (H1481, H168) — who may be a GUEST in Your tent? gur is the resident-alien verb; even the welcomed are lodgers in God's house. mi-yishkon be-har qodshekha (H7931, H2022, H6944): who may settle, take up tabernacle-residence, on the holy hill. Psalm 24:3 asks it again.

2.text: The one who walks in wholeness, who does what is right, and who speaks the truth inside his own heart;
2.amp: He that walks [halak] uprightly [tamim — whole, blameless], and works [paal] righteousness [tsedek], and speaks [dabar] the truth [emeth] in his heart [lebab].
2.notes: Three verbs, whole life: holekh tamim (H1980, H8549), walking whole — integrity as gait; poel tsedek (H6466, H6664), doing right as work; dover emeth bi-lebabo (H1696, H571, H3824), speaking truth IN his heart, before any mouth is involved. The liturgy starts with the man nobody sees.

3.text: who does not go slandering with his tongue, who does no harm to his neighbor, and who will not pick up a reproach against the one near him;
3.amp: He that backbites [ragal — goes about on foot, spies out, slanders] not with his tongue [lashon], nor does [asah] evil [ra] to his neighbour [rea], nor takes up ['receiveth, or, endureth', nasa, the KJV margin] a reproach [cherpah] against his neighbour [qarov — the one near].
3.notes: lo-ragal al-leshono (H7270, H3956): ragal is the spy's verb — to go about on foot, reconnoitering — so slander is pictured as a tongue out patrolling for material. lo asah ra le-reehu (H6213, H7451, H7453), and cherpah lo-nasa al-qerovo (H2781, H5375, H7138): he will not even pick up, carry, a reproach against the one near him — the passive gossip who merely repeats is disqualified too.

4.text: in whose eyes a vile man is despised, but who honors those who fear the LORD; who swears to his own hurt and will not change it;
4.amp: In whose eyes [ayin] a vile person [maas — one rejected, worthless] is contemned [bazah — despised]; but he honours [kabad] them that fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH]. He that swears [shaba] to his own hurt [raa], and changes [mur] not.
4.notes: nivzeh be-enav nimas (H959, H5869, H3988): the rejected man is despised in his eyes — his admiration is calibrated to God's, not to wealth or rank — ve-et-yire YHWH yekhabbed (H3373, H3513), and he gives weight to the God-fearers. nishba le-hara ve-lo yamir (H7650, H7489, H4171): swears to his own loss and will not swap it out — the man whose word costs him and holds (cf. Matthew 5:37).

5.text: who does not lend his money at interest, and does not take a bribe against the innocent. The one who does these things will never be shaken.
5.amp: He that puts not out [natan] his money [keseph] to usury [neshek — interest that bites], nor takes [laqach] reward [shochad — a bribe] against the innocent [naqi]. He that does [asah] these things shall never [olam] be moved [mot].
5.notes: kaspo lo-natan be-neshek (H3701, H5414, H5392): neshek is from the root 'to bite' — interest that takes a bite out of a poor brother (cf. Exodus 22:25); shochad al-naqi lo laqach (H7810, H5355, H3947), no bribe against the innocent. Then the promise: oseh-elleh lo yimmot le-olam (H6213, H4131, H5769) — never shaken. The guest who lives like this on God's hill finds the hill holds him up.
